content: Six-axis robots (UR included) have 3 singularity types: wrist (axes of J4 and J6 become parallel/coincident), shoulder (wrist center aligns with J1 axis), elbow (wrist center coplanar with J2/J3, arm fully extended/flexed, theta3 = 0 or pi). At a singularity there are infinite IK solutions for the same tip position; if the wrong one is chosen, joints can be commanded to spin unexpectedly fast even though the end-effector barely moves. Elbow singularity is easiest to detect/avoid; shoulder is hardest since it's not a single-joint condition.
